details: Bitcoin experienced a significant drop, falling below $60,000 to its weakest price since October 2024, before recovering to trade around $63,000. This downturn was largely influenced by a stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs report, which fueled expectations of continued hawkish monetary policy from the Federal Reserve, leading to broader market sell-offs and substantial Bitcoin ETF outflows. Geopolitical tensions, such as those involving Iran, also contributed to market fragility.
title: Bitcoin Recovers Slightly After Dropping Below $60,000 Amid Macroeconomic Concerns

details: The Kingdom of Bhutan has reportedly offloaded 738 Bitcoin, worth approximately $44.88 million, amidst Bitcoin's dip to the $60,000 level. This sovereign drawdown adds to the selling pressure in the market.
title: Bhutan Sells Off 738 Bitcoin Valued at $44.88 Million

details: Charles Hoskinson, the founder of Cardano, has suggested the possibility of splitting the Cardano blockchain. This statement comes with a warning that more applications built on the network might fail. Such a move could have significant implications for the Cardano ecosystem and its investors.
title: Cardano Founder Hints at Potential Blockchain Split

details: Following Bitcoin's struggle, major memecoins Dogecoin and Shiba Inu have seen significant declines, with both diving approximately 9%. The performance of memecoins often mirrors the broader crypto market, amplifying movements seen in Bitcoin.
title: Memecoins Dogecoin and Shiba Inu Dive Amid Bitcoin's Slide

details: While the broader market faces headwinds, several altcoins have posted gains. Flare (FLR) jumped over 3% driven by FAssets v1.3 and FXRP tag minting promotion. TRON (TRX) rose 3% following a new Bitnomial listing and treasury purchases. Filecoin (FIL) gained 6% amid a broader market rebound and a short squeeze.
title: Flare (FLR), TRON (TRX), and Filecoin (FIL) Show Positive Movements
